cs.title: CS / Software
ap: AP Calculus BC — the de facto standard for top CS applicants. If only AB is offered, take AB and consider self-studying BC
AP Computer Science A — directly tied to the major. Even if not offered, self-study is relatively easy, so it's the #1 candidate for a self-study exam
AP Physics 1 (or C) — strengthens engineering-side credibility
AP Statistics — more valuable if you're heading toward AI/data
cs.strong: Math is 80% of it. Reaching Calculus by 12th grade is effectively the required line, then physics

guide.label: Spike type
guide.text: Personal projects that leave a deliverable — a deployed app/website, a GitHub portfolio. "Does it have users?" separates project tiers

guide.label: External validation type
guide.text: USACO (free, online, open to international students) / hackathons / submission-based contests like the Congressional App Challenge

guide.label: Pitfalls
guide.text: Piling up unfinished projects, mistaking a paid coding bootcamp certificate for an achievement

guide.label: direct-admit Warning
guide.text: Many schools admit CS by major, and competition is far tougher than the school's overall acceptance rate. Internal transfer is also hard — checking how your target schools select is a must-do item

academic: Check your math track — confirm the path to Calc by 12th grade (fix the track with summer acceleration if needed)
activity: Python basics + first mini project (goal: graduate from following tutorials)

academic: Take AP CS A or start self-studying
Lock in 11th-grade Calc (BC preferred) registration
activity: Open a GitHub portfolio, get 1 project to deployed state
First USACO Bronze attempt (no pressure — gauge your level)

academic: AP Calc BC + Physics (if you have room)
Check direct-admit status for every target school
activity: Get real users for your flagship project
Try to move up in USACO, or 1 hackathon/submission-based contest
Lead a team or club

academic: Take a post-Calc course if offered (otherwise maintain)
Keep 12th-grade grades up
activity: Tidy up portfolio links (README, demo video)
Prepare a tech-stack summary for the application's Additional Info

engineering.title: Engineering (Mechanical, Electrical, Chemical, Aerospace, etc.)
ap: AP Calculus BC
AP Physics C: Mechanics (mechanical/aerospace) or AP Chemistry (chemical) — pick 1 to match your sub-field
AP Physics C: E&M (electrical direction)
AP CS A — a plus across modern engineering
engineering.strong: Math and physics are the top two. Only for ChemE is chemistry on par with physics

guide.label: Spike type
guide.text: Build-and-break projects — robots, drones, 3D printing, Arduino. Recording the process (build log) matters as much as the result

guide.label: External validation type
guide.text: Robotics competitions (FTC/VEX, etc. — if your school has no team, founding one is itself a leadership story), F=ma and physics olympiads, Science Olympiad

guide.label: Pitfalls
guide.text: Unclear role in a team competition ("team member 1"). You need to be able to say what part you owned

academic: Check your math track (same as CS — reaching Calc is a must)
Build physics fundamentals
activity: Intro to making — Arduino, 3D printing, assembly projects; get in the habit of keeping a build log

academic: Lock in the 11th-grade AP Physics (C or 1, matching your direction) + Calc lineup
If ChemE, prioritize Chemistry
activity: Join a robotics team — if there isn't one, prepare to found it (founding is the bigger story)
Take part in Science Olympiad-type events

academic: AP Calc BC + AP Physics C (or Chem) at the same time — the heaviest year for this major
activity: Secure a clearly defined part on the team (design/coding/drive, etc.)
Sit competitions like F=ma
Finish 1 personal build

academic: Maintain physics and math rigor
activity: Organize a portfolio of your builds (photos, build log, results)
Reflect competition results in your application

business.title: Business / Economics
ap: AP Micro + Macro Economics — the set directly tied to the major, and relatively easy to self-study
AP Calculus AB or higher — top colleges see economics as close to a math major. BC is even better
AP Statistics
AP English Language — the major leans heavily on case analysis and essays
business.strong: Math (especially for the economics direction), English writing

guide.label: Spike type
guide.text: Hands-on operating experience — even something small with real money, customers, and results (running a school store, selling merch, handling social media marketing for a local shop)

guide.label: External validation type
guide.text: DECA/FBLA (found a chapter if your school has none), Wharton Global High School Investment Competition (free, online, team-based), economics divisions of essay contests

guide.label: Pitfalls
guide.text: Titles with no execution, like "member of the entrepreneurship club." An activity with real numbers — even 10,000 won in revenue — wins

academic: Keep up your math track (view econ as a math major)
Build an English writing foundation
activity: Small hands-on experience — school sales, joining a fundraiser to get a feel for it

academic: Take AP Econ (Micro/Macro) or plan to self-study
Lock in 11th-grade Calc registration
activity: Check for a DECA/FBLA chapter — if none, push to found one
Plan a hands-on project (one with real money and customers)

academic: AP Calc AB/BC + Statistics
English Language
activity: Enter a team competition like the Wharton investment competition
Produce numbers for the project you're running (revenue, users, growth rate)

academic: Maintain math rigor
activity: Quantify project results for your application ("X won in revenue, Y customers")
Name a successor to prove continuity

math_data.title: Math / Statistics / Data Science
ap: AP Calculus BC — stopping at AB in this major is close to a negative signal
AP Statistics
AP CS A — near-essential for the data direction
If your school offers post-Calc courses (multivariable, etc.), top priority; if not, keep a record of online coursework
math_data.strong: Staying on the top math track is everything. If you've exhausted your school's math courses, continuing on your own from there is the spike

guide.label: Spike type
guide.text: Math/data projects — real-data analysis reports, simulations, math tutoring and educational content

guide.label: External validation type
guide.text: The AMC → AIME line (open to international students; secure a testing site in advance), Kaggle-type data competitions, submitting to student journals

guide.label: Pitfalls
guide.text: Giving up on this major because your AMC score isn't there — competitions are just one path of many; the project/research path is equally valid

academic: Stay on the top math track — in this major, the track itself is the credential
activity: First AMC 8/10 attempt (to gauge your level)
Start math club activities

academic: Lock in 11th-grade Calc BC registration
Consider AP Statistics alongside
activity: Retake AMC 10/12 — go for the AIME cutoff
First data project (1 real-data analysis)

academic: AP Calc BC + Statistics + CS A combination
If you've exhausted school math, take further courses online
activity: Attempt AIME, or Kaggle/data competitions
Cover the leadership axis with math tutoring/educational content

academic: Continue post-Calc courses (multivariable, linear algebra, etc.)
activity: Organize project and competition results
If you have research, wrap up a student journal submission

natural_sci.title: Natural Sciences (Physics, Chemistry, Biology)
ap: The science AP for your direction (Physics C / Chemistry / Biology) — the 1 for your own direction is a must
1 more adjacent science AP (e.g., chemistry if you're a biology major)
AP Calculus (BC recommended for physics/chemistry; AB + Statistics is also valid for biology)
natural_sci.strong: That science + math. Physics and chemistry depend on math far more than biology does

guide.label: Spike type
guide.text: Research experience — it doesn't have to be a fancy lab. Self-designed experiments, data collection projects, and literature reviews are all valid starting points

guide.label: External validation type
guide.text: The science fair line (school → regional → international), Science Olympiad, submitting to high school journals (JEI, etc.) — submission costs almost nothing and leaves a deliverable, the best value path

guide.label: Pitfalls
guide.text: Listing "completed a research program" itself as an achievement. Without what you discovered/built, completion isn't a credential

academic: Work diligently on the 3 core sciences — you don't need to pick a direction yet
Check your math track
activity: Explore areas of interest — science club, in-school lab activities, find your direction through documentaries and books

academic: Settle your major direction, then register for that AP science in 11th grade
Lock in your Calc path
activity: Start a self-designed experiment/data collection project
Take part in Science Olympiad and the school science fair

academic: AP science for your direction + Calc — BC for physics/chem; AB + Stat combination possible for biology
activity: Deepen research → enter a regional science fair or submit to a student journal (JEI, etc.)
Consider adding an adjacent science AP

academic: Adjacent science AP, or maintain rigor
activity: Wrap up research deliverables (reflect publication/entry results in your application)
Hand down your lab know-how to younger students

premed.title: Health / Pre-med Track
ap: AP Biology
AP Chemistry — the dual must-have axis for pre-med
AP Psychology — relevant to health fields + light load
AP Statistics — foundation for medical research
premed.strong: Biology, chemistry, and GPA itself (the pre-med track is a fight over college grades, so AOs look at grade consistency too)

guide.label: Spike type
guide.text: Sustained activity caring for people — hospital clinical volunteering is hard for high schoolers to access in Korea, so regular volunteering at nursing homes or disability welfare centers, organizing blood drives, and creating health education content are realistic alternatives

guide.label: External validation type
guide.text: HOSA (you can found a school chapter), the biology olympiad line, health-topic research and journal submissions

guide.label: Pitfalls
guide.text: Using a one-off medical mission trip as your spike. AOs rate 2 years of weekend volunteering above 2 weeks of overseas service

academic: Solid biology and chemistry fundamentals
GPA habits — on this track, grade consistency is life
activity: Secure a regular volunteering site (a sustainable one like a nursing home or welfare center) — design a 2-year routine, not a 2-week event

academic: Lock in 11th-grade AP Bio or Chem registration
activity: Keep volunteering + grow your role (participant → organizer)
Check for a HOSA chapter / consider founding one

academic: Whichever of AP Bio + Chem you haven't taken + reinforce with Psychology/Statistics
activity: Health-topic research or organize a campaign (blood drive, health education content)
Organize your cumulative volunteer hour records

academic: Maintain science rigor + defend GPA
activity: Shape your volunteering narrative — not the hour count but "why did you keep going" as essay material
Hand off your ongoing activity

social_sci.title: Social Sciences (Politics, Psychology, International Relations)
ap: AP Psychology (psychology direction) / AP US Gov or Comparative Gov (politics/international direction)
AP World History or AP European History
AP Statistics — a choice that shows you see social science as a data discipline
AP English Language
social_sci.strong: History and social studies, English reading and writing

guide.label: Spike type
guide.text: Evidence of digging into a question — survey-based original research, running a current-affairs blog/newsletter long-term, community campaigns

guide.label: External validation type
guide.text: MUN (chairing or founding is a different tier from just participating), debate tournaments, essay competitions (John Locke, etc.), student journalism

guide.label: Pitfalls
guide.text: Listing how many MUNs you attended. Growth in role (delegate → chair → organizer) is the narrative, not the count

academic: Foundation in history and social studies + build up English reading volume
activity: First MUN/debate participation (gauge your level)
Pick an issue you care about

academic: Lock in 11th-grade AP registration for your direction (Psych/Gov/History)
Consider Statistics
activity: Start growing your role in MUN/debate
Launch content on your issue (blog, newsletter)

academic: AP for your direction + AP Statistics (signals social science = data discipline) + English Lang
activity: Go for chair/organizing roles, or run your own survey study
Enter essay competitions (John Locke, etc.)

academic: Maintain rigor
activity: Organize research and campaign results
Reflect the cumulative record of your long-running content (issue count, subscribers) in your application

humanities.title: Humanities (Literature, History, Philosophy)
ap: AP English Literature + AP English Language — the top two for humanities applicants
AP World/European History
A foreign language AP (if your school offers one) — strengthens humanities credibility
Don't drop math either — top colleges look at math rigor even for humanities applicants (at least AB recommended)
humanities.strong: English, history, and — surprisingly — keeping up math rigor

guide.label: Spike type
guide.text: A body of writing — a long-term writing project (fiction, nonfiction, criticism), founding/running a literary magazine or school paper, independent publishing

guide.label: External validation type
guide.text: Scholastic Art & Writing Awards (check in advance whether international students may enter), John Locke essay, The Concord Review (history papers — highest difficulty), literary journal submissions

guide.label: Pitfalls
guide.text: "I read a lot" is not an activity. You need proof that what you read turned into what you wrote

academic: Foundation in English and history + the habit of turning reading into records (reviews, notes)
activity: Start with the school paper or literary magazine — if there isn't one, founding it is the best story

academic: Lock in 11th-grade AP English Lang + History registration
Keep math on the AB line too
activity: Start a long-term writing project (serialized fiction, nonfiction, criticism)
Enter your first writing competition

academic: AP English Lang + History for your direction (+ foreign language AP if possible)
activity: Enter competitions in earnest — Scholastic, John Locke, etc.
Finish your writing project or become editor-in-chief of the literary magazine

academic: Wrap up AP English Lit
activity: Finish your flagship piece — the source for application supplements and essays
If history is your direction, consider attempting the Concord Review

arts.title: Art / Design
ap: AP Art & Design (2-D / 3-D / Drawing to match your direction) — it's structured around a portfolio submission, so it's itself a process of building up work
AP Art History
1-2 core academic APs — art programs at comprehensive universities look at academics too (less weight if you're applying only to art schools)
arts.strong: Studio art + defending core GPA when applying to comprehensive universities

guide.label: Spike type
guide.text: The portfolio matters more than the activity list — unique to this major. Start building up work from 10th grade, start editing from the summer of 11th. Submitting 15-20 pieces at application time is standard

guide.label: External validation type
guide.text: Scholastic Art & Writing, open competitions, exhibitions (organizing a school exhibition has the double effect of leadership + exposure for your work)

guide.label: Pitfalls
guide.text: A portfolio rushed together hagwon-style right before applications — US art programs look at consistency of perspective more than technical polish

academic: Set a core GPA defense line (in case you apply to comprehensive universities)
Keep taking art classes
activity: The year to make "a lot" of work — style experiments, a sketchbook habit

academic: AP Art History or 1 core AP
activity: Officially start building up portfolio work
First competition entry, e.g., Scholastic

academic: Start AP Art & Design (tied to your submission portfolio)
activity: Narrow your artistic world — produce a series on a consistent theme
Organize a school exhibition (double effect: leadership + exposure)

academic: Complete the AP Art & Design portfolio
activity: Edit 15-20 pieces for your application portfolio (from summer)
Check every target school's portfolio requirements — they differ by school

undecided.title: Undecided
undecided.strong: Math and English — the two axes that are a foundation whichever major you pick

guide.label: A balanced combination across the 4 core subjects that keeps the door open to any major
guide.text: AP Calculus (starting with AB) + AP English Language + 1 science + 1 history/social studies

guide.label: Principle
guide.text: The more undecided you are, the more it's about balanced core rigor over going all-in on one field. But "undecided" doesn't mean "slack" — take the highest difficulty your school offers in each core

guide.label: Exploration strategy
guide.text: In grades 9-10, try 2-3 activities of different kinds (making / people / writing) → narrow to 1-2 by the end of 10th grade. "Exploring" isn't a weakness if it's a planned process

guide.label: Pitfalls
guide.text: Still spreading wide into 11th grade — miss the moment to narrow and there's no time left to build a spike. The tool's grade rollover is the device that flags this timing

academic: Balance across the 4 cores + invest first in math and English
activity: Try 2-3 activities of different kinds (1 each: making / people / writing)

academic: Take the highest difficulty your school offers in the cores
Make 11th-grade APs the "combination that works for any major" (Calc + Eng Lang + 1 science + 1 history)
activity: The narrowing year — compress to 1-2 by the end of 10th grade (the tool prompts you to reset your major at this point)

academic: Reorganize APs around your compressed direction — from here on, follow that major's table
activity: Go deeper in the activities you kept — this is where you build the spike (apply that major's 11th-grade track)

academic: Apply that major's table
activity: Apply that major's table
The "exploration → choice process" itself can be a narrative in your essays

architecture.title: Architecture
ap: AP Calculus (AB or BC) — many B.Arch and architectural engineering programs require math, and it prepares you for structures courses
AP Physics 1 (or C) — foundation for structures and mechanics
AP Studio Art: Drawing or 2-D — directly tied to portfolio building
AP Art History — the language of architectural history and criticism
architecture.strong: Both math and art — B.Arch (5-year) requires a portfolio; architectural engineering within an engineering school weighs math and physics heavily

guide.label: Spike type
guide.text: Portfolio — observational drawings, models, spatial sketches. Many schools ask for work that shows hand drawing and your thought process rather than software renderings (check each school's portfolio requirements)

guide.label: External validation type
guide.text: Official university summer architecture programs (e.g., Cornell Summer College Architecture, Carnegie Mellon Pre-College Architecture — check each university's official page) / the Architecture & Industrial Design category of the Scholastic Art & Writing Awards

guide.label: Pitfalls
guide.text: Collecting nothing but rendering images; checking portfolio requirements (page count, format, deadline) for the first time in the fall of 12th grade

guide.label: direct-admit Warning
guide.text: Most B.Arch programs admit directly at the department level + portfolio review (some interview) — deadlines and requirements differ from the general application. First confirm whether your target school is B.Arch (5-year) or BS/BA in Architecture (4-year, portfolio optional)

academic: fall
activity: spike | T | Start a sketchbook — observational drawings of nearby buildings and spaces | An architecture portfolio starts with "can you see?" — hand drawing is the first material

academic: summer
activity: validation | T | Research university summer architecture programs and prepare applications | Official university programs like Cornell and CMU — attending the summer of 11th grade is typical; applications are in spring

academic: summer
activity: spike | T | Complete 5 core portfolio pieces | Summer is the only long stretch of production time

academic: fall
activity: story | F | Edit the portfolio per school + check separate deadlines | Some schools have a portfolio deadline that differs from the application deadline

nursing.title: Nursing
ap: AP Biology — many direct-entry nursing (BSN) programs require high school biology
AP Chemistry — likewise, a chemistry requirement is common
AP Statistics — preparation for nursing statistics courses
AP Psychology — a prerequisite at some programs
nursing.strong: Biology and chemistry — many direct-entry BSN programs explicitly require high school biology, chemistry, and math (check each school)

guide.label: Spike type
guide.text: Sustained volunteering with patient contact — hospitals, nursing homes, community health. At an international school, health clubs and Red Cross activities can substitute. Continuity over hour count

guide.label: External validation type
guide.text: HOSA–Future Health Professionals competitions (international chapters operate) / CPR and first-aid certification / official university nursing summer programs

guide.label: Pitfalls
guide.text: Confusing this with pre-med prep — nursing centers on direct entry to a 4-year BSN, so you need to commit to the major at application time. Just piling up volunteer hour numbers

guide.label: direct-admit Warning
guide.text: Many BSN programs are direct-entry (selected at admission) with small cohorts, so acceptance is far lower than the school's overall rate, and entering after enrollment is also hard. Confirm whether your target school is direct-entry BSN or 2+2 (apply after enrollment)

academic: fall
activity: spike | T | First experience with a health club or volunteering | In nursing, the spike is a "record of caring for people" — the earlier you start, the more continuity you build

academic: spring
activity: rigor | F | Lock in 11th-grade AP Biology and Chemistry registration | The two core courses for direct-entry BSN requirements

academic: summer
activity: leadership | T | Grow your volunteering role — participant → planning/teaching | Same principle as pre-med: 2 years of weekend volunteering > a 2-week event

academic: fall
activity: story | F | Prepare cumulative volunteering records and a science teacher recommendation | Both numbers and narrative — "why nursing" from your records

media.title: Communication / Media (Communication, Media, Journalism)
ap: AP English Language and Composition — the basics of argument and writing
AP English Literature — text analysis
AP U.S. Government or Comparative Government — current-affairs and political context
AP Psychology — foundation for communication theory (if offered)
media.strong: English (writing) — your portfolio and essays are the evidence

guide.label: Spike type
guide.text: Consistent publishing — regularly running a school newspaper, magazine, podcast, or video channel; reporting and editing roles. "Regularity" separates the tiers

guide.label: External validation type
guide.text: Scholastic Art & Writing Awards (journalism/essay categories) / student press competitions (NSPA, CSPA, etc., if you're on a school publication) / official university summer journalism programs (e.g., Northwestern Medill Cherubs — check each university's official page)

guide.label: Pitfalls
guide.text: Chasing only view and follower counts; deliverables with no record of the reporting and editing process

guide.label: direct-admit Warning
guide.text: At some schools the journalism/communication school admits separately — check how your target school's program is housed and how you apply

academic: fall
activity: spike | T | Start participating in school media (newspaper, broadcast, magazine) | The media major's spike is a "record of publishing regularly"

academic: spring
activity: validation | T | First Scholastic Art & Writing entry (journalism/essay) | Open to international students; deadlines every fall-winter

academic: summer
activity: spike | T | Personal media project, or organize 5 flagship pieces | Deliverables you can show via a link bring the activities section to life

academic: fall
activity: story | F | Edit 3-5 flagship pieces + prepare links for the application | In a form that can go straight into the application's Additional Info and portfolio links

psychology.title: Psychology
ap: AP Psychology — directly tied to the major. Relatively easy to self-study, so a top candidate for a self-study exam even if not offered
AP Statistics — signals you know psychology runs on statistics
AP Biology — worth more if you're heading toward neuroscience or clinical
AP Calculus AB (BC if possible) — reinforces a BS/data-leaning direction
psychology.strong: Statistics and research experience are the core — 'interested in people' is only a starting point; evidence that you tested a question with data is what separates tiers

guide.label: Spike type
guide.text: A survey or behavioral-observation study you designed yourself — however small, carried through collect → analyze → conclude. Or a long-running peer mental-health campaign or education content

guide.label: External validation type
guide.text: Student journal submissions (e.g., JEI) / science fair behavioral & social science category / psychology essay and research competitions

guide.label: Pitfalls
guide.text: Mistaking reading lots of psychology books for an activity, or imitating 'counseling' without qualifications (an ethics problem) — aim for research, education, and campaigns, not counseling

academic: Build your biology and math base + English reading volume
activity: Pick a question you care about (e.g., sleep and focus, social media and mood)
Explore with intro content and books — keep short notes on what you read

academic: Lock in AP Psychology and Statistics for 11th grade
activity: First mini survey study — carry it through collect → analyze → short report
Start a mental-health campaign or peer education activity

academic: AP Psych + Statistics (+ Bio if heading toward neuroscience)
activity: Scale up the research — submit to a student journal or enter a science fair
Grow your role in the campaign/education work (participant → organizer)

academic: Keep rigor up
activity: Wrap up research and campaign results — put cumulative numbers (sample size, issues published) on the application
